_meta.title: Push-surface ratchet ceilings (#1273)
_meta.description: Anti-regrowth ratchet on the always-pushed context layer. Each surface has two ceilings (items and bytes); the guard fails red when a surface exceeds either. CONTEXT.md as a whole file is deliberately NOT capped (see context_md_whole_file).
_meta.item_definition: An 'item' is a line whose stripped form is a bullet ('- ', '* ', or '+ ' at any nesting depth) or a numbered list line ('N. ' or 'N) '). Block-level HTML comments (<!-- ... -->) are excluded before counting. Fenced code, YAML frontmatter, and .claude/rules/* files without a paths: key are all COUNTED — they are pushed at session start. This definition is load-bearing and is asserted by a synthetic-fixture test in tests/ci/test_push_surface_guard.py.

margin.statement: Ceilings = per-surface 90-day maximum (git-history max over the last 90 days, computed at fixture-writing time 2026-07-31, except invariants_md which is a new file created 2026-08-07 by #1417 — its ceiling is measured-at-creation + 20% margin) + 20% margin, rounded up. #1417 retired the SessionStart hook's budget-constrained CONTEXT.md push (context_md_pushed, dropped in 47% of sessions) in favor of static files delivered via bare @import — invariants_md (30 items/5,359 bytes) — which carry their own ceilings under the same 20%-margin policy, no longer bounded by ASSEMBLY_BUDGET_CHARS.
margin.uuids: Each surface entry carries the record_decision UUID that set its ceiling (adjacent comment), per the Quota-Probe.ps1 precedent. Bumping a ceiling without a fresh record_decision UUID is a review failure.

provenance.source: Issue #1273 records aggregate 90-day maxima of 129 items / 49,632 bytes across the four source files. Per-surface ceilings here are computed from per-surface git-history maxima: soul_md 38/9512, project_claude_md 65/25283 (pre-#1252 compression), userlevel_claude_md 30/16498, userlevel_doctrine_md 9/6870 (file created 2026-07-30, max == current). #1417 (2026-08-07) replaced context_md_pushed with two @import-delivered files: invariants_md 30 items/5,359 bytes measured-at-creation, glossary_index_md 8 items/1,104 bytes measured-at-creation. #1418 (2026-08-07, decision d7df1c94-4102-435c-a994-e629220e0335) retired glossary_index_md entirely — a category index of where to look does not clear the always-loaded admission bar (ff994ca2), so it was replaced by a pull pointer in CLAUDE.md and its surface row deleted.
provenance.basis: post-compression sizes (#1265-#1268 closed); #1417 extraction for invariants_md

_meta.same_pr_raise: The JSON IS the fixture: the guard reads ceilings only from this file, so raising a ceiling is impossible without editing it in the same PR. Regrowth is therefore a reviewable act.

context_md_whole_file.note: CONTEXT.md as a whole file has NO ceiling — pull-only Glossary bodies may grow freely (that is the push/pull split). The formerly-pushed Invariants now live in their own ratcheted file — see surfaces.invariants_md — delivered via @import instead of the SessionStart hook assembler. The Glossary is fully pull-only again since #1418 retired its always-loaded category index.

fanout_budget.statement: Every byte of the inherited layer -- both CLAUDE.md levels plus every bare @import reachable from them -- is paid N+1 times on a fan-out of N subagents (measured in #1270; see docs/research/context-management.md A.7). SessionStart hook output is NOT inherited and is excluded. The inherited set is DERIVED by walking bare imports, never hardcoded, so a newly added import is charged automatically. Ceiling = measured bytes + 20% margin, rounded up -- same margin policy as the per-surface ceilings. Raising this ceiling requires editing this fixture in the same PR, which is the point: the raise makes the N+1 cost visible at review time.
fanout_budget.raise_history: Created 2026-08-07 at 43,043 measured / 51,652 ceiling. Raised the same day by #1426 to 60,270 measured / 72,324 ceiling (+17,227 B/agent, 401,180 B at the reference fan-out of 6). The raise is exactly the cost the creation-time statement predicted for #1426 (~16.5 KB): SOUL.md (9,596) and DOCTRINE.md (6,870) were never actually delivered, so they had never been charged. Two independent defects hid them, both of the same silent-nothing shape: the imports were written mid-prose with a glued trailing comma and did not resolve, and _resolve_import in the guard normalized with str.lstrip('./') -- a character SET -- which ate the leading dot of .claude-userlevel/SOUL.md and silently dropped both from the walk. This is not context regrowth; it is previously-uncounted delivery becoming real and visible.
fanout_budget.no_per_agent_profile: #1324 AC3, answered NO with a documented negative: Claude Code exposes no frontmatter field or per-agent setting to give subagents a stripped-down CLAUDE.md. Explore and Plan are the only subagents that omit CLAUDE.md and that is not configurable. Budgeting is therefore the only lever.

soul_md.note: Identity. Loaded via a bare `@SOUL.md` import in .claude-userlevel/CLAUDE.md, not a SessionStart hook step (#1328). #1328 asserted this delivery but did not achieve it: the import was written mid-prose and never resolved, so no session loaded SOUL.md until #1426 made the line bare. This note describes what now happens, not what always did.

project_claude_md.note: Repo rules. Loaded by the harness into every jarvis session.

userlevel_claude_md.note: User-level CLAUDE.md source (installer source, not the repo-local mirror). Loaded into every session on every device.

userlevel_doctrine_md.note: Shared cross-repo norms, @import-ed from user-level CLAUDE.md. Same correction as soul_md: #1315 wrote the import mid-prose, so it never resolved and this file reached no session until #1426 made the line bare.

invariants_md.note: Extracted ## Invariants, delivered via a bare @docs/context/invariants.md import in CLAUDE.md — replaces the SessionStart hook's context_md_pushed surface (#1417). Ceiling = measured-at-creation 30 items / 5,359 bytes + 20% margin, rounded up. Not bounded by ASSEMBLY_BUDGET_CHARS — @import bypasses the assembler entirely.
